ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the rectangle $ABCD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. After folding $\triangle ABE$ along $BE$, we obtain $\triangle GBE$. Extending $BG$ intersects $CD$ at point $F$. If $CF=2$ and $FD=4$, what is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect EF, \\
$\because$ $CF=2$, $FD=4$, \\
$\therefore$ $CD=CF+FD=2+4=6$, \\
$\because$ the quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ $AB=CD=6$, \\
As known from the folding, $EG=EA$, \\
Also, $\because$ E is the midpoint of AD, \\
$\therefore$ $ED=EA$, \\
$\therefore$ $ED=EG$, \\
$\because$ $EF=EF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EGF \cong \triangle EDF$ (HL), \\
$\therefore$ $GF=DF=4$, \\
By the property of folding: $BG=AB=6$, \\
$\therefore$ $BF=BG+GF=6+4=10$, \\
$\therefore$ $BC=\sqrt{BF^{2}-CF^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-2^{2}}=\boxed{4\sqrt{6}}$.

In the figure there is the folded point G, line segments BE and EG have been drawn, and the line from B through G is extended to point F on the right side CD; F is between C and D, and the problem gives CF=2, FD=4. According to the method, draw the auxiliary line EF. Reasoning: From CF=2, FD=4, obtain CD=CF+FD=6. Because ABCD is a rectangle, AB=CD=6. When triangle ABE is folded to triangle GBE, A corresponds to G, therefore BG=BA=6, EG=EA, and the original right angle ∠BAE is folded to ∠BGE, so EG is perpendicular to BG; also because B, G, F are collinear, EG is perpendicular to GF, and triangle EGF is a right triangle. On the other hand, in the rectangle ED is perpendicular to DF, so triangle EDF is also a right triangle. Because E is the midpoint of AD, EA=ED; also EG=EA, so EG=ED. The two right triangles EGF and EDF have the common hypotenuse EF, and one right leg EG=ED, therefore by HL it can be obtained that △EGF≅△EDF, and thus GF=DF=4. In the figure B, G, F are collinear and G is between B and F, so BF=BG+GF=6+4=10. In right triangle BCF, BF is the hypotenuse, CF=2, therefore BC=√(BF^2−CF^2)=√(10^2−2^2)=√96=4√6.
